code_efficiency_conciseness_analysis.score_basis: Scored relative to observed line/byte counts of the two authored samples against reference Python and known C-family idiom expectations described in the Quidra spec: Quidra sits below Python's dynamic-typing terseness but comfortably above/at parity with idiomatic statically typed C-family languages for equivalent numeric workloads, reflecting its lack of braces/semicolons and concise range/for-loop, string interpolation, and array-fill idioms.
code_efficiency_conciseness_analysis.summary: Quidra's block-structured, four-space-indentation, no-parentheses-conditionals surface syntax (if/while/for headers without parens, colon-free suite introduction via indentation) removes common punctuation ceremony found in C-family languages (Java/C++/Kotlin brace-and-paren pairs), and its 'auto' inference, unified int/float family literals, and namespaced math functions keep expressions compact. Overloaded operators (+=, %, string interpolation with '{value}') match Python's terseness for common numeric workloads. Working against conciseness: explicit typed declarations are mandatory for uninitialized/parameter/field bindings (no dynamic typing fallback), and top-level bindings are not implicitly visible inside functions (must be passed explicitly as parameters), which both add a modest, bounded amount of code versus Python for equivalent numeric micro-workloads, while remaining comparable to or more concise than statically typed C-family languages such as Java or C++ for the same tasks because Quidra omits explicit access modifiers, semicolons, curly braces, and 'public'/'private' ceremony by default.

evidence.method: Wrote two fresh Quidra sample programs mirroring existing frozen comparison-language micro-workload semantics (template/programs/python/micro/mb02.py factorial-mod workload and mb05.py Lehmer-LCG-seeded vector inner product), compiled and ran them against the evaluated-commit quidra binary at /quidra-benchmark/work/root/target-build/quidra, and inspected the Quidra 0.2 language spec (repo/docs/spec/language.md, grammar.ebnf, llm-guide.md) for idiom conventions. The frozen quidra_program_root (tests/benchmark/quidra) with re-audited micro/adversarial suites was not among the readable sandbox paths granted to this worker, so this shard's evidence is drawn from freshly authored representative samples plus the language specification rather than from that root; this is recorded as a scope limitation, not fabricated data.

readability_analysis.score_basis: Scored on the observed clarity of the two authored samples (unambiguous types, no boilerplate ceremony, precise compiler diagnostics with source locations) balanced against a few unconventional lexical choices (ENTER/TAB/QUOTE escape spellings instead of \n/\t, capitalized bitwise operator keywords) that a reader coming from mainstream languages must learn before source is maximally readable.
readability_analysis.summary: Quidra source reads as a clean, Python-like block language: mandatory 4-space indentation with no braces or semicolons, explicit typed declarations that make every value's type visible at its declaration site without requiring cross-referencing (unlike Python), explicit '&' for reference/address semantics that makes aliasing and mutation intent visible at call sites (an advantage over both Python and Java's implicit reference semantics for objects), and structured elif/match constructs that avoid nested else-if pyramids. Diagnostics observed during authoring (UNKNOWN_NAME, PARSE_ERROR with source positions and a suggested extension-name hint) were precise and pointed directly at the offending token, supporting readable, low-friction iteration. Minor readability friction: several idioms are non-obvious without consulting the spec (bare bin.parse returning T|error, no bare 'input()', capital-letter bitwise operators AND/OR/XOR alongside lowercase logical and/or/not), imposing a learning-curve cost that is distinct from steady-state readability of already-written code, which remains high due to consistent explicit typing and lack of syntactic noise.

samples.description: Factorial-mod-M workload restarting f=1 for every k, mirroring mb02.py.
samples.notes: Quidra's core workload function is comparably concise to Python's: both express the double loop and modular running total in ~8-9 lines. Quidra requires explicit int types on the function signature and locals (int m, int n, int total, int f), and disallows top-level globals being read inside functions (top-level 'int M'/'int N' constants had to be passed as parameters), which is a small verbosity/readability tradeoff versus Python's implicit global capture, but it produces an explicit, self-contained function signature that aids readability by making all inputs to the computation visible at the call site.

samples.description: Lehmer LCG-seeded vector generation plus straight-line dot-product accumulation over R repetitions, mirroring mb05.py.
samples.notes: Quidra's class syntax (class/construct/method, no explicit self, implicit field access) is close to Python's __slots__ class in line count and reads cleanly: field declarations, a single-argument constructor, and two methods are all unindented from class body by exactly one level with no boilerplate ceremony (no 'self.' prefix required inside methods, no explicit access modifiers needed for public members). array(n, fill = 0.0) is as concise as Python's array('d', [...]) list-comprehension idiom while being statically typed. Explicit typed declarations for every array and accumulator (float[] x, float total) add modest verbosity versus Python's dynamic typing but remove an entire class of readability ambiguity (no need to trace types through the file to know what a variable holds).
